timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream is transport-only in the review ledger; it accounts for relay/session traffic without projected semantic task actions.
Session index records the Kimi session used by the parallel run and contains no projected semantic task actions.
Background probe child built a 195-case corpus and SPEC under /tmp/test20, verified many jsonschema edge cases, and returned a detailed findings summary without writing /output.
Engine and assembly child probed reference behavior, wrote errors.mjs, engine.mjs, and drafts.mjs, found several integration mismatches, partially edited the resolver, then was cancelled.
Scalar keyword child probed type, enum, const, numeric, and string behavior, wrote core/numeric/string keyword modules, scratch-tested them, and completed.
Array keyword child probed items, prefixItems, uniqueItems, contains, and crash behavior, wrote array.mjs, ran differential checks, and completed.
Object keyword child probed properties, dependencies, required, propertyNames, and related counts, wrote object.mjs, syntax-checked it, and completed.
Applicator keyword child probed allOf, anyOf, oneOf, if/then/else, unevaluated behavior, wrote applicator.mjs, mock-tested it, and completed.
Meta-schema child wrote meta/schemas.mjs, built a scratch checker, verified 45 schema cases, imported the module, and completed.
Support and entrypoint child wrote formats, validatorFor, errortree, argparse, and test20.mjs, ran stub and real integration checks, found two unresolved end-to-end mismatches, and was cancelled.
Parallel parent entered swarm mode, launched one background probe and a seven-agent implementation swarm, then was cancelled as the swarm returned five completed and two aborted children.

parallel.requirements: Parallel recognized the prompt's ESM, .mjs, CLI, /output, no external dependencies, and executable-observation requirements, and decomposed jsonschema behavior into keyword, engine, meta, support, and corpus areas.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent launched a background corpus probe plus a seven-agent implementation swarm. Children owned files by module family: engine/assembly, scalar, array, object, applicator, meta-schemas, and support/entrypoint.
parallel.implementation: Completed children wrote keyword modules and meta schemas, the engine child wrote and edited core validator files, and the support child wrote the entry point plus CLI and ErrorTree helpers. Tests exposed unresolved engine, draft integer, and ErrorTree mismatches before cancellation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The shared /output tree contained the expected entry and library files, but final integration was not completed by the parent after receiving the swarm result; two children were aborted while their fixes were still in progress.
parallel.verification: Children ran many local probes, mock tests, and limited end-to-end diff batteries. The background 195-case corpus stayed in /tmp and was not consumed by the parent, and the final whole-system rerun was interrupted.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official parallel evaluation failed 0 of 58 samples. Observable unfinished work includes cancelled engine/support bug fixing, unresolved end-to-end mismatches, and no parent-level acceptance pass after the swarm returned.

serial.requirements: Serial recognized the same ESM, .mjs, no-external-dependency, manual CLI, /output placement, exact output, and executable-probing requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor retained ownership of probing, module design, implementation, differential testing, and final fixes without child delegation.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote a monolithic but structured library set, including type helpers, equality, meta checking, keyword engine, draft classes, ErrorTree, format checker, custom JSON parser, and test20.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial integrated its modules itself and artifact validation found test20.mjs plus the supporting library files. There was no cross-agent merge, though a helper compare.sh was also delivered.
serial.verification: Serial built and repeatedly ran a large compare.sh differential harness against the executable, improved from 92/102 to 101/102 self-checks, and identified the remaining 3.0 integer mismatch before timeout.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official serial evaluation also failed 0 of 58 samples. The raw trajectory shows one remaining differential mismatch at the last compare pass and no final post-fix completion before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel identified the same Python-to-Node.js ESM port requirements and delegated jsonschema behavior coverage across specialized child scopes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial identified the same requirements and kept them in one local implementation plan.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The recognized task obligations were materially the same; the difference was execution strategy rather than prompt comprehension.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work into one background probe plus seven child implementation scopes under a shared contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept probing, implementation, integration, and testing under one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit multi-owner module boundaries; serial had a single owner for the whole implementation pipeline.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied a shared module contract and per-file ownership, but child findings and the completed corpus did not reach a final parent integration loop.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained executable observations and implementation assumptions in one trajectory and revised modules directly from those findings.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel context problem was not an absent initial contract; it was result lifecycle and parent monitoring after children produced findings.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented separate component files for engine, draft assembly, keywords, meta schemas, support helpers, and test20.mjs, with some files produced by children that later completed and two by children that aborted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented its own cohesive library set and rewrote affected modules after comparing against the executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel implementation was assembled from concurrently written components; serial implementation was revised as one integrated codebase.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The background probe completed and two implementation children were aborted as the swarm returned near cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to retrieve and kept its own compare/fix state in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child result lifecycle failures; serial's remaining defects were local implementation closure rather than child handoff loss.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a shared /output tree from multiple live children. Artifact validation copied all expected files, but support testing still observed unresolved integrated mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and revised one integrated output tree itself and included a compare harness in the final artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel integration depended on cross-child timing and final parent reconciliation that did not happen; serial integration defects stayed inside one local loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children verified slices and one support child ran an end-to-end battery that still had two failures; the parent did not complete a final acceptance pass.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran its compare.sh harness, fixed most failures, and ended with one known mismatch in a 101/102 self-test pass.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's verification loop was more integrated and further reduced known failures; parallel verification was fragmented and interrupted before final acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after launching eight total children, with the implementation swarm reporting aborted children and the parent cancelled.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but with one active owner and no child cancellations.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the run budget, but parallel closed with incomplete child lifecycles and an unused completed probe result.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations show both parallel and serial failed all 58 samples, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The serial run nevertheless reached a clearer local stopping point, reducing its own differential harness to one known mismatch. The parallel run produced more component artifacts but had two aborted implementation children, did not consume the completed behavioral corpus, and did not complete parent-level integration verification. These are adverse parallel process differences but not an observed pass/fail differential.
parallel_contributors: Parallel component work was interrupted while engine and support children still had unresolved end-to-end mismatches.
The completed background corpus/spec was returned but not used for parent-level final verification or fix prioritization.
serial_contributors: Serial retained a single implementation and verification loop and reduced its local compare harness to one remaining mismatch.
Serial also timed out and officially failed all samples, so its better local trajectory did not become a passing solution.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial built a custom JSON parser to preserve Python int/float token distinctions; parallel support identified the 1.0 draft4 integer mismatch but did not finish a fix.
Parallel support identified ErrorTree dedup behavior, while serial implemented and tested a similar fix before its last compare pass.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported comparative process contrast only

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership existed across engine, support, and keyword children; the observed failures came from cancellation and unused results.
Engine/assembly and support/entrypoint scopes included integration responsibilities, so integration was not left wholly unowned.
The support child owned test20.mjs and artifact validation found the expected entry point and library files.
The parent and support child planned end-to-end tests; the breakdown was cancelled execution and unconsumed results, not an absent pipeline owner.
Implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; the parent launched implementation children while the probe child ran in background.
Investigation did not complete as a separate first phase before productive implementation; probing and implementation overlapped.
There is no separate proof that auxiliary work starved the critical path; the directly observed adverse boundary is child cancellation.
The broad swarm ended in timeout, but that same chain is captured more directly as Early Child Termination rather than a separate load label.
Engine and support scopes were broad, but the retained boundary is explicit cancellation before finalized fixes, not one demonstrably oversized child scope.
The child prompts gave concrete file responsibilities, draft behavior, interfaces, and testing expectations; no parent-known requirement omitted from an initial brief is proven.
The shared prompt specified filenames, exports, imports, error shape, validator API, and keyword contract; unresolved behavior was unfinished fixes, not absent interface contract.
No known finding is shown being truncated or lost in transfer before a receiver repeated work or acted without it.
The probe result was available as a summarized completed result; the problem was nonuse, not excessive volume that the parent unsuccessfully tried to reduce.
No child or parent action is shown consuming a superseded workspace, requirement, dependency, or decision state.
Although children found contract mismatches, there were not incompatible returned handoffs that the parent received and failed to adjudicate before acting.
The parent did not present the whole task as complete; the run ended by timeout and cancellation, with official evaluation closing the cell.
There was no replacement child or retry that repeated prior work without inherited findings, checkpoints, or current file state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: Two active implementation children were explicitly cancelled before their required engine/support fixes had finalized, after live integration tests showed unresolved mismatches.
candidates.realized_consequence: Required engine and support/entrypoint bug-fix scopes were interrupted, leaving the parallel artifact without the identified fixes or a final integrated rerun.
candidates.near_match_reason: No Failure Takeover describes the same cancellation chain downstream; the directly observed boundary is early termination of active children.

candidates.reason: There was no complete directly promotable candidate; unresolved mismatches and cancelled child work remained before any final placement could be completed.
No child result was merged only after a successful integrated verification; instead verification was still failing and child work was interrupted.
Completed child implementations were written into /output and artifact validation copied them; the issue was unfinished cancelled children and unused probe results.
The behavioral probe result did reach the parent as a completed task notification, so its nonuse is classified as Unused Completed Result.
Cancelled children were part of the same chain retained as Early Child Termination, with no separate post-cancel recovery window before global timeout.
A completed background probe returned a verified 195-case behavioral corpus and SPEC, but the parent never used it for final integration or acceptance checks.
candidates.realized_consequence: The verified probe corpus and SPEC stayed outside /output and did not inform the parent's final integration, so known behavioral findings were not applied to acceptance decisions.
candidates.near_match_reason: The result was not trapped below the parent; it returned as a completed task notification but was not inspected or used.

candidates.reason: The waiting-to-timeout symptoms overlap with the retained cancelled-child and unused-result episodes, and no distinct wait-only episode is needed.
Children wrote distinct assigned module files; unresolved behavior required integration, but no competing cross-file design collision is proven.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source or configuration file and then reconciling a same-file race.
No child replaced or deleted another actor's non-entry source file; file ownership was mostly disjoint.
Only the support child is shown writing the test20.mjs deliverable, so no uncoordinated entrypoint overwrite occurred.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple final outputs or invalidated another actor's final-tree provenance.
Multiple live agents shared /output, but the concrete adverse events were cancellation and unconsumed results rather than unstable provenance from shared writes.
No generated cache, fixture, temporary path, or auxiliary artifact from one actor is shown contaminating another actor's probing or validation.
